The provided statements establish a collection of direct ancestor-descendant links. By chaining these links using transitivity, a single consistent path is obtained:

Nathan is an ancestor of Brenda, who is an ancestor of Richard, who is an ancestor of Steven, … (continuing through every intermediate individual named in the statements) … who is an ancestor of Jennifer, who is an ancestor of Gerald.

Consequently Gerald lies on the descendant side of Nathan, i.e., Gerald is Nathan’s descendant. No opposing chain from Gerald back upward to Nathan exists, so the opposite relation (option 4) is ruled out. The statements supply no information about any person above Nathan or below Gerald; therefore whether Gerald and Nathan share any additional common ancestor or common descendant cannot be determined from the given data. The only definitively supported relationship among the five choices is therefore option 1.
